claims.text: Z.ai released GLM-5 on 2026-02-12 and described it as targeting complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks.
The first-party release describes 744B total parameters with 40B active, 28.5T pre-training tokens, DeepSeek Sparse Attention integration, and asynchronous RL infrastructure named slime.
The released weights are described as MIT licensed with deployment paths through frameworks including vLLM and SGLang.
Benchmark rankings and claims that GLM-5 closes the gap with frontier proprietary models are vendor claims.

limitations: Architecture/training figures are first-party technical disclosures, not independently audited.
The model’s release and license can be verified independently from its claimed performance.
overrides.why_this_special: GLM-5 is a major February open-weight model whose stated target—complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks—closely matches the month’s broader agentic-engineering convergence.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material February 2026 technical change.

claims.text: ComfyUI v0.15.0 was published on 2026-02-24 and included native text-generation support, audio-related nodes, API-node additions, and image/video workflow changes.
v0.15.1 followed on 2026-02-26 as the next patch in the same line.
Performance fixes or improvements described in release notes are project claims unless independently measured.

limitations: The retained series contains only v0.15.0 and v0.15.1, while the repository had multiple February releases; it should not be presented as a complete monthly changelog.
The release is broad and incremental rather than a single month-defining architectural milestone.
overrides.why_this_special: Useful ecosystem context showing ComfyUI expanding across text, audio, hosted model nodes, and image/video workflows, but not strong enough to become a core February story.
overrides.rationale: Retain as supporting/background evidence; do not allocate a standalone core story unless Architecture needs it.

artifact.canonical_name: OpenAI Codex February stack: app, GPT-5.3-Codex, System Card, and Codex-Spark

claims.text: OpenAI introduced the Codex app on 2026-02-02 as a workspace for managing multiple coding agents and long-running parallel work.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5.3-Codex on 2026-02-05 for coding plus longer-running research, tool use, and complex execution tasks.
The GPT-5.3-Codex System Card was published on 2026-02-05 and applies OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework cybersecurity evaluation to the model.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark on 2026-02-12 as a research-preview model designed for realtime coding interaction.
Claims such as GPT-5.3-Codex being 25% faster and Codex-Spark exceeding 1,000 tokens/s on Cerebras hardware are vendor-reported performance claims.

limitations: The Evidence task intentionally groups four related first-party items; drafting must keep product, base model, system-card, and specialized Spark boundaries explicit.
Performance and benchmark comparisons are vendor-reported.
Codex-Spark’s throughput statement depends on specialized Cerebras hardware and research-preview conditions.
Cyber capability classification must reproduce the System Card’s stated threshold/precaution boundary rather than exaggerating it.
overrides.why_this_special: The clearest February package showing coding moving from a single model toward a persistent agent workspace, long-running tool-using execution, explicit cyber-risk evaluation, and a low-latency interactive variant.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material February 2026 technical change.

claims.text: Transformers v5.2.0 was published on 2026-02-16 with explicit support additions for VoxtralRealtime, GLM-5, Qwen3.5/Qwen3.5 MoE, and the VibeVoice Acoustic Tokenizer.
The VoxtralRealtime implementation describes streaming ASR using an audio encoder plus Mistral-based language-model decoder with time conditioning and causal-convolution caches.
Transformers v5.1.0 was published earlier in February and included additional model-family integrations such as GLM-OCR.
Vendor performance descriptions quoted inside the Transformers release notes are not independent Hugging Face validation.

limitations: Framework integration proves implementation/support landed in Transformers; it does not independently validate the model vendors’ benchmark claims.
v5.1.0 is supporting context; v5.2.0 is the materially stronger February integration milestone.
The v5.2 release also contains breaking interface changes, so model support should not be reduced to a simple compatibility list.
overrides.why_this_special: Transformers v5.2 is unusually useful ecosystem evidence because one mid-February release integrates GLM-5, Qwen3.5, Voxtral Realtime, and VibeVoice components, showing how rapidly the model-release wave entered the common implementation layer.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material February 2026 technical change.

claims.text: vLLM v0.16.0 was published on 2026-02-25; its release notes state that the branch was cut on 2026-02-08.
v0.16.0 added a WebSocket-based Realtime API with streaming-audio/Voxtral realtime support, Responses API improvements, tool-calling fixes, unified parallel drafting, and major XPU changes.
The release reports 30.8% end-to-end throughput improvement and 31.8% TPOT improvement for async scheduling plus pipeline parallelism; these are project-reported measurements.
v0.15.1 was published on 2026-02-04 and serves as earlier-month context, but v0.16.0 carries the stronger February systems signal.

limitations: The v0.16.0 branch-cut date means it cannot be used as evidence that every late-February model change was already integrated.
Performance figures are project release-note measurements and are not independently reproduced.
The series groups one patch and one major release; architecture should center v0.16.0.
overrides.why_this_special: vLLM v0.16.0 provides strong systems evidence that realtime audio, Responses/tool APIs, speculative decoding, parallel scheduling, and heterogeneous hardware support were becoming first-class serving concerns in the same month.
overrides.rationale: Primary-source evidence supports Candidate Selection for a material February 2026 technical change.
